box.explanation: Creates an axis-aligned rectangular solid with gmsh.model.occ.addBox from a minimum corner and three extents in millimetres, as the solid source for a tetrahedral node. Choose it for test domains, channel sections and mesh-size studies where no CAD file is needed; its exact volume and bounds let verification compare the mesh with analytic values. Use cylinder, hollowCylinder or sphere for those primitives, or readSTEP for other shapes. The solid is not published by itself; only the tetrahedral node publishes files.
pitfalls: size holds extents, not the opposite corner; origin is the minimum corner.
faceGroups coordinates are absolute, so moving origin moves the face planes they must match.

examples.purpose: Mesh a 10 mm cube and independently verify its 1000 mm^3 volume.

readSTEP.explanation: Imports exactly one solid from a single-file STEP document with gmsh.model.occ.importShapes, converting its length unit to millimetres. Choose it to mesh a real CAD part, such as a FreeCAD STEP artifact in a workflow. The file bytes are captured (digest and retained copy) before meshing, and the volume and bounds measured by OpenCASCADE become the reference for verification. Feature history and STEP labels are not imported; name faces with the tetrahedral faceGroups.
pitfalls: The path must be absolute and end in .step or .stp, with at most 16 MiB; multi-solid files and assemblies fail during meshing.
Native acceptance covers STEP parts exported by FreeCAD (20×10×5 and 20×10×7 mm); STEP from other CAD tools has not had a Schemaxis acceptance check.

examples.purpose: Mesh a STEP solid exported by FreeCAD and inspect the result in ParaView.

tetrahedral.explanation: Meshes the preceding solid with first-order (4-node) tetrahedra using the chosen Delaunay or HXT 3D algorithm at a global target size, optionally finer near named boundaries, and assigns one named physical volume plus named planar face groups, named whole analytic cylindrical wall groups (bore wall, hole wall, shaft surface) with a proven material side, and a remainder boundary that may be empty when those groups cover the whole boundary. It publishes result.msh (ASCII MSH 2.2 with names), volume.vtu and boundary.vtu (numeric physicalTag per cell, with quality arrays on the volume) and mesh-summary.json (name and tag map, mm units, counts, CAD and mesh volume, quality distributions). Every mesh is reopened in a fresh Gmsh process and checked independently for positive volumes, a closed boundary, face membership and agreement with the CAD volume; every boundary triangle of a named wall is re-proven from coordinates, with measured chord deviation. Add the top-level refinement object to refine until measured requirements pass.
pitfalls: size is a target edge length in mm, not a guarantee of element count, maximum edge length or shape quality.
The VTU files carry numeric tags only; keep mesh-summary.json for group names and units.
Outputs are bounded to 50000 nodes and 200000 cells, linear elements only, and no boundary conditions are applied.
Name a cylindrical wall with cylinderGroups, not faceGroups; only typed analytic world-axis cylinders are selectable (see cadSurfaces in mesh-summary.json).
Chord deviation falls roughly with the square of the edge length; a requirement tighter than the cell budget allows ends a refinement study with STUDY_REQUIREMENTS_NOT_MET.

examples.purpose: Mesh a 10 mm cube with default group names.
Name two opposite x faces and refine the mesh near one of them.
Name two caps, a bore and an outer wall; the remainder is empty.
FreeCAD plate with two equal bores, one named per hole, with local sizing near one.

cylinder.explanation: Constructs a full right circular cylinder as one solid for tetrahedral meshing. origin is the centre of the starting disk, axis chooses a positive world direction, radius and height are in millimetres. Use this for rods and cylindrical specimens without a CAD file; choose hollowCylinder for a through bore. The host independently checks CAD volume pi*r²*h, analytic bounds and radial containment of every mesh node. The solid is consumed by tetrahedral; it is not separately published. Linear triangles approximate circular caps and the lateral surface. Name the lateral wall with tetrahedral cylinderGroups (side outer, radius equal to this radius, centre equal to origin) to apply loads or constraints by name.
pitfalls: A target mesh size is not a geometric-error guarantee; inspect the independently measured volume error.
Named circular or annular planar caps require an explicit areaTolerance; the strict default detects their discretisation loss.

examples.purpose: Editable millimetre-scale cylinder mesh with analytic acceptance checks.

hollowCylinder.explanation: Constructs a straight annular solid by subtracting a coaxial through cylinder from a larger cylinder, consuming both tools and requiring exactly one resulting volume. Use it for tubes and sleeves without authoring a boolean tree. origin is the starting annulus centre; axis is positive x, y or z. radius is the outer radius, innerRadius the bore radius; their difference must be at least 0.001 mm. Independent verification checks pi*(radius²-innerRadius²)*height, bounds and each node against the outer radius and bore. Both curved walls remain in the remainder boundary group unless you name them with tetrahedral cylinderGroups (bore: side inner at innerRadius; outside: side outer at radius), which also lets the remainder be empty when the caps are named too.
pitfalls: A target mesh size is not a geometric-error guarantee; inspect the independently measured volume error.
Named circular or annular planar caps require an explicit areaTolerance; the strict default detects their discretisation loss.

examples.purpose: Editable millimetre-scale hollowCylinder mesh with analytic acceptance checks.
Fully named sleeve: caps, bore and outer wall with references keeping selectors in step with the dimensions.

sphere.explanation: Constructs one complete spherical solid from a centre and radius in millimetres for tetrahedral meshing. Use it for spherical specimens and curved-boundary resolution studies. The host independently checks 4*pi*r³/3, analytic bounds and radial containment of every mesh node. It is a full ball, with no polar cuts, shell thickness or planar caps. Linear boundary triangles inscribe an approximation; choose a small enough mesh size to meet volumeTolerance.
pitfalls: A sphere has no planar faces; keep its surface in the remainder group.

examples.purpose: Editable millimetre-scale sphere mesh with analytic acceptance checks.

fields.explanation: A Gmsh meshing document: one solid source node (box, cylinder, hollowCylinder, sphere or readSTEP) followed by one tetrahedral node, run in an isolated Gmsh 4.15.x Python process. A successful run publishes result.msh (ASCII MSH 2.2 with named physical groups), volume.vtu, boundary.vtu and mesh-summary.json, after the mesh has been reopened in a fresh Gmsh process and checked independently (positive cell volumes, closed boundary, face membership, volume against CAD). Add the optional refinement object to mesh repeatedly at smaller sizes until declared quality or resolution requirements pass.
pitfalls: The document prepares a mesh only: face and volume names are labels for a downstream solver; no materials, loads or boundary conditions are assigned.
Every length in the document is in millimetres; there is no unit conversion for authored values.

/properties/version.explanation: Identifies the document format and chooses its adaptor. Keep the version matching the selected schema.

/properties/units.explanation: Declares that every authored length (box origin and size, element sizes, face-group coordinates and tolerances, sizing distances and refinement lengths) is in millimetres, and that published meshes are in millimetres. Only "mm" is accepted. For readSTEP, Schemaxis sets Gmsh's Geometry.OCCTargetUnit to MM before import, so OpenCASCADE converts the STEP file's declared length unit to millimetres.
/properties/units.label: Length units
/properties/units.defaultMeaning: Required; there is no default. Any other value fails planning with UNSUPPORTED_UNITS.
pitfalls: The STEP conversion relies on the unit declared in the file; a part saved with the wrong unit imports at the wrong scale. Check cadBounds and cadVolume in mesh-summary.json.

/properties/nodes.explanation: The meshing chain, which always has exactly two nodes in a fixed order: first the solid source (box, cylinder, hollowCylinder, sphere or readSTEP), then the tetrahedral node whose inputs.input names the first node. Node ids must be distinct. Any other count or order fails planning with INVALID_DOCUMENT or INVALID_DEPENDENCY.
/properties/nodes.label: Nodes
pitfalls: To mesh a different shape, replace the first node (for example box by readSTEP) rather than adding a third node.

/properties/nodes/items.explanation: One node of the two-node meshing chain. Its filter selects the operation: box, cylinder, hollowCylinder, sphere or readSTEP is only valid in the first position and tetrahedral only in the second.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0.explanation: Choose the box node when the domain is a rectangular block that you can describe by a corner and three extents, such as a test domain, channel section or mesh-size study. Because its volume and bounds are known exactly, verification also compares the mesh with the analytic volume and bounds. Choose another typed primitive or readSTEP for other shapes.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.

Position and extents of the axis-aligned box, both in millimetres. size decides the domain and, together with the tetrahedral size, the number of cells; origin only moves the box, which also moves the planes used by faceGroups. Omitted settings take the Schemaxis defaults: origin [0, 0, 0] and size [10, 10, 10].

World coordinates [x, y, z] of the box's minimum corner; the box extends from origin to origin + size along each positive axis. Schemaxis passes these as the x, y, z arguments of gmsh.model.occ.addBox. Moving the origin changes the coordinates of every box face, so faceGroups coordinates must move with it.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.label: Minimum corner
pitfalls: faceGroups coordinates are absolute: with origin [-5, 0, 0] and size [10, 10, 10], the x faces lie at x = -5 and x = 5, not 0 and 10.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: One coordinate of the minimum corner in millimetres; its position in the array selects the axis (first x, second y, third z).

Extents [dx, dy, dz] of the box along x, y and z, each positive. These are lengths, not the opposite corner. Verification checks that the CAD volume equals dx·dy·dz and that the mesh bounds equal origin and origin + size. Larger extents at the same element size mean more cells: planning rejects the document with RESOURCE_LIMIT when 6 × Π(extent / smallest element size + 1) exceeds 200000.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.label: Box extents
pitfalls: A box from (5, 0, 0) to (15, 10, 10) is origin [5, 0, 0] with size [10, 10, 10]; entering [15, 10, 10] doubles the x extent.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: One positive extent of the box in millimetres; its position in the array selects the axis (first x, second y, third z).
Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1.explanation: Choose the readSTEP node to mesh an existing CAD part, for example a STEP file exported by FreeCAD earlier in a workflow. The file must hold exactly one solid; Schemaxis captures its bytes before meshing and uses the volume and bounds measured by OpenCASCADE as the reference for the volume and bounds checks. Choose box when the domain is a simple block.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.

The STEP import has a single required setting, the file. Import behaviour is fixed by Schemaxis: lengths are converted to millimetres, only the highest-dimension entities (solids) are imported, and the format is forced to STEP.

Absolute path of a single-file STEP (ISO 10303-21) document containing exactly one solid. The name must end in .step or .stp (any letter case); relative paths fail planning with INVALID_RESOURCE. Before meshing, Schemaxis checks that it is a regular file of at most 16 MiB that begins with "ISO-10303-21;", records its SHA-256 digest and meshes a retained copy (source.step) in the run directory. In a workflow the path can come from an upstream CAD artifact, such as {"$artifact": "cad", "index": 0}.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1/properti.label: STEP file
pitfalls: Assemblies or files with several solids are refused with UNSUPPORTED_RESOURCE ("STEP input must contain exactly one solid volume") located at this file option; export one fused solid.
Editing the file changes its digest: earlier results are not reused, and a refinement study fails if the bytes change between attempts.
Feature history and STEP face labels are not imported; name faces with faceGroups instead.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1/properti.explanation: Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2.explanation: The meshing node. It must be the second node, reference the solid node through inputs.input, and be the node selected by output. It turns the solid into first-order tetrahedra with named physical groups and publishes the mesh, two VTU views and a summary.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.

Settings for the tetrahedral mesh. The global size has the largest effect on cell count and on how well curved faces are approximated; faceGroups and nearBoundaries name planar faces and refine near them; volumeTolerance sets the volume acceptance check. Omitted settings take the Schemaxis defaults (size 3 mm, names "domain" and "boundary", no face groups or local sizing, volumeTolerance 0.01). Schemaxis sets the relevant Gmsh mesh options itself and does not read Gmsh configuration files.

Global target edge length of the tetrahedra. Schemaxis passes it to Gmsh as Mesh.MeshSizeMax (and as Mesh.MeshSizeMin when no nearBoundaries rule is smaller) with sizes from CAD points, curvature and boundary extension disabled, and meshes with the selected Delaunay or HXT 3D algorithm. Smaller values give more, smaller tetrahedra (the count grows roughly with the inverse cube of size) and follow curved faces more closely, because curvature-based sizing is off.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Target element size
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 3 mm. Gmsh's own Mesh.MeshSizeMax default (1e+22) never applies because Schemaxis always sets it.
pitfalls: It is a target, not a bound: individual edges can be longer. Use refinement.requirements.maximumEdgeLength when a bound matters.

A size that is small relative to the solid is rejected when the estimate 6 × Π(bounding-box extent / smallest size + 1) exceeds 200000. For a box this fails planning with RESOURCE_LIMIT; for readSTEP the bounds are only known after import, so the Gmsh worker refuses with RESOURCE_LIMIT ("requested mesh size exceeds the 200000-cell work estimate") located at the tetrahedral size. Increase size either way.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Name of the physical volume group (tag 1) that contains every tetrahedron of the solid. The name is stored in result.msh and mesh-summary.json; the VTU files carry only the numeric physicalTag 1. Names start with an ASCII letter followed by letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, and must differ from boundaryName and every faceGroups name.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Volume group name
pitfalls: Spaces, dots or non-ASCII characters fail planning with INVALID_ARGUMENT even though the form accepts any text; use names such as fluid_region.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Name of the physical surface group (tag 2) that holds every boundary face not selected by faceGroups, or the entire exterior surface when faceGroups is empty. nearBoundaries and refinement boundary requirements can refer to it. The same naming rules as volumeName apply, and all group names must be distinct.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Remainder boundary name
pitfalls: Tag 2 always means the remainder group whatever its name; tools reading the VTU files must map physicalTag to names through mesh-summary.json.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Up to 12 named physical surface groups (shared with cylinderGroups), each holding the whole CAD faces that lie flat on one axis-aligned plane (for example x = 0). Groups receive tags 3, 4, … in list order, and every face not selected goes to boundaryName (tag 2). Use them to name inlets, outlets, fixed or loaded faces for later setup. Each selector must match at least one face, selectors on the same axis must not overlap, and at least one face must remain for the remainder group.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Planar face groups
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: [] (no face groups; the whole exterior belongs to boundaryName).
pitfalls: Naming all six faces of a box leaves no remainder and is refused with INVALID_SELECTION ("leave at least one face for the remainder boundary group"). The remainder may be empty only when cylinderGroups are declared and, together with the plane groups, name the whole boundary.
Planar groups select planes only; name a cylindrical wall with cylinderGroups (typed analytic cylinders on a world axis). Other curved or oblique faces always belong to the remainder group.
Reordering the list changes the numeric tags written to the VTU files.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: One named plane selector. Every boundary face whose extent along axis stays within tolerance of coordinate joins this group, so several separate faces on the same plane are grouped together.

Physical surface name written to result.msh and mesh-summary.json. It must start with an ASCII letter followed by letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, and be unique among volumeName, boundaryName and the other face groups. nearBoundaries and refinement boundary requirements refer to the group by this name.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Group name
pitfalls: A name such as "x min" (with a space) fails planning with INVALID_ARGUMENT; use x_min.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: World axis perpendicular to the selected plane: x selects faces of constant x, y faces of constant y, z faces of constant z. Pick the axis the face is normal to, not an axis lying within the face.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Normal axis
pitfalls: For the top face of a box spanning z = 0 to 5, use axis z with coordinate 5.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Position of the plane along axis, in world millimetres (after STEP unit conversion, and including any box origin). A face is selected when both its minimum and maximum bounding-box coordinates along axis lie within tolerance of this value.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Plane coordinate
pitfalls: If no face lies on the plane, meshing is refused with INVALID_SELECTION ("face selector … is empty"), located at that faceGroups entry; check cadBounds in mesh-summary.json or the CAD model coordinates.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Absolute distance allowed between a face's extent along axis and coordinate when selecting faces; verification uses the same distance when it classifies every boundary triangle. Increase it, within 1e-6 to 1e-3 mm, only when a face that sits slightly off the nominal plane is not found. Two selectors on the same axis are rejected as overlapping when their coordinates differ by no more than the sum of their tolerances.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Plane tolerance

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Up to 13 rules that request a finer target size close to named boundary groups. For each rule Schemaxis builds a Gmsh Distance field to that group's surfaces and a Threshold field: the size equals the rule's size on the surface, grows linearly to the global size at the rule's distance, and stays at the global size beyond. Rules are combined with a Min field, so the smallest requested size wins where they overlap. The native field settings are read back and verified.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Local boundary sizing
pitfalls: The RESOURCE_LIMIT estimate assumes the smallest rule size fills the whole bounding box, so a small local size on a large part can be rejected although the real mesh would fit.
In a refinement study the rule sizes shrink with the global size (not below 0.001 mm) but the distances stay fixed.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: One sizing rule for one named boundary group: the target size on that boundary and the distance over which the size grows back to the global size. Each boundary name may appear in only one rule.

Name of the boundary group to refine near: boundaryName (the whole remaining exterior) or one faceGroups name. Gmsh resolves the name to that physical group's CAD surfaces, so native face numbers are never authored.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Boundary group
pitfalls: An undeclared name, a repeated name or volumeName fails planning with INVALID_SELECTION.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Target tetrahedron edge length on the named surfaces (the Threshold field's SizeMin). It must not exceed the tetrahedral size; a value equal to it has no local effect. The smallest rule size also becomes Mesh.MeshSizeMin and is the size used by the cell-count estimate.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Size at boundary
pitfalls: It is a target, not a bound; check the achieved value with refinement.requirements.boundaryMaximumEdgeLength or quality.boundaries in mesh-summary.json.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Distance from the named surfaces at which the target size has grown back to the global size (Threshold DistMax, with DistMin 0 and StopAtDistMax off). Between the surface and this distance the size is interpolated linearly. Larger distances spread fine elements deeper into the volume and increase the cell count. Distances are measured to 20 sample points per direction on each surface (Distance field Sampling 20), so the transition is approximate.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Transition distance
pitfalls: Refinement studies scale rule sizes but not this distance; set it for the finest mesh you expect to accept.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Largest allowed relative difference between the total tetrahedral volume and the CAD volume measured by OpenCASCADE: |Vmesh − Vcad| ≤ volumeTolerance × Vcad. Solids bounded only by planar faces, such as a box, are filled exactly by linear tetrahedra, so tiny values such as 1e-6 are appropriate; curved faces are approximated by flat triangles and the error shrinks as size decreases. A mesh outside the tolerance fails verification and is not published.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Volume tolerance
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.units: Dimensionless fraction of the CAD volume (0.01 = 1 %)
pitfalls: In a refinement study this remains a hard check: a candidate outside it stops the study with a fault instead of being refined. Use refinement.requirements.maximumVolumeRelativeError for a criterion that drives refinement.
If it fails on curved CAD, reduce size or investigate the CAD; do not loosen it beyond what your analysis can accept.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.
Id of the solid node (the box, cylinder, hollowCylinder, sphere or readSTEP node in the first position) to be meshed. Any other value fails planning with INVALID_DEPENDENCY.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Solid

/properties/output.explanation: Id of the node whose results are published; it must be the tetrahedral node. The published artifacts are, in order: result.msh, volume.vtu, boundary.vtu and mesh-summary.json, followed by study-summary.json and study.html when refinement is present. Workflow steps select them by zero-based index, for example index 1 for volume.vtu.
/properties/output.label: Output node
pitfalls: Selecting the box or readSTEP node fails planning with INVALID_SELECTION; solids are not published on their own.

/properties/refinement.explanation: Optional bounded refinement study. The first candidate uses the authored size; each candidate is meshed, verified and measured, and the first one that meets every requirement within maxTetrahedra is accepted. Otherwise the global size is multiplied by reductionFactor (not below minimumSize) and meshing repeats. The study stops on acceptance, after maxIterations candidates, after a candidate at minimumSize, when the cell budget is exceeded, or when the next candidate would exceed the native work estimate. If no candidate passes, the run fails with STUDY_REQUIREMENTS_NOT_MET, keeps study-summary.json and study.html, and exports no mesh.
/properties/refinement.label: Refinement study
/properties/refinement.defaultMeaning: Omitted: a single mesh at the authored size, with no requirement checks beyond verification.
pitfalls: A smaller size does not guarantee better element shape, so a strict minimumMeanRatio can exhaust the study.
The accepted mesh is the first passing candidate, not the coarsest or optimal one; every candidate shares one run timeout.

/properties/refinement/properties/maxIte.explanation: Largest number of candidate meshes in the study, counting the first one at the authored size; 1 only checks the authored mesh against the requirements. Each candidate is a full native mesh and verification, so higher values cost more time within the same timeout.
/properties/refinement/properties/maxIte.label: Maximum candidates

/properties/refinement/properties/reduct.explanation: Multiplier applied to the global size between candidates: next size = max(previous size × factor, minimumSize). nearBoundaries sizes are scaled by the same ratio. Smaller factors reach fine meshes in fewer candidates but can step past the coarsest acceptable mesh; values near 0.95 take small steps and need more candidates.
/properties/refinement/properties/reduct.label: Size reduction factor

/properties/refinement/properties/minimu.explanation: Smallest global size the study may try. The last candidate is clamped to this size, and once a candidate at or below it has been tested the study stops. It must not exceed the tetrahedral size (INVALID_STUDY otherwise).
/properties/refinement/properties/minimu.label: Smallest global size
pitfalls: The default is not a recommendation; on larger parts a small minimum is usually cut short by the 200000-cell work estimate. Set it to the finest mesh you are prepared to run.

/properties/refinement/properties/maxTet.explanation: Largest number of tetrahedra an acceptable candidate may have. It is checked after meshing: a candidate that exceeds it is rejected and the study stops instead of refining further. The native hard limits of 200000 cells and 50000 nodes apply independently.
/properties/refinement/properties/maxTet.label: Tetrahedron budget
pitfalls: If the authored size already exceeds the budget, the study stops after its first candidate; increase size or the budget.

/properties/refinement/properties/requir.explanation: Measured criteria that a candidate must all satisfy; at least one is required and only the declared ones are checked. Comparisons are inclusive, and the measurements are made by Schemaxis from the retained mesh coordinates, independently of Gmsh.
/properties/refinement/properties/requir.label: Acceptance requirements
/properties/refinement/properties/requir.defaultMeaning: Required whenever refinement is present; an empty object fails with INVALID_STUDY.
pitfalls: These describe mesh size, shape and volume only; they do not establish solution accuracy or solver convergence.

/properties/refinement/properties/requir.explanation: Upper bound on the longest edge of any tetrahedron in the mesh (quality.maximumEdgeLength.maximum in mesh-summary.json). The global size is only a target, so use this when a resolution limit must actually hold; the study refines until the longest edge is no greater than this value.
/properties/refinement/properties/requir.label: Maximum edge length

/properties/refinement/properties/requir.explanation: Lower bound on the worst tetrahedron's mean ratio, 12·(3V)^(2/3) / Σ(edge length²): 1 for a regular tetrahedron, tending to 0 for a flat sliver. Schemaxis also reports a diagnostic count below 0.2, but that is not an acceptance threshold; choose the bound your downstream solver needs.
/properties/refinement/properties/requir.label: Minimum mean ratio
pitfalls: Reducing size does not necessarily improve the worst element, so a strict bound may never be met; inspect worstCells in mesh-summary.json.

/properties/refinement/properties/requir.explanation: Upper bound on |Vmesh − Vcad| / Vcad as a study criterion: a candidate above it is rejected and refined. This differs from the tetrahedral volumeTolerance, which is a hard check that fails the run, so set this at or below volumeTolerance; a larger value has no effect.
/properties/refinement/properties/requir.label: Maximum volume error
/properties/refinement/properties/requir.units: Dimensionless fraction of the CAD volume (0.001 = 0.1 %)

/properties/refinement/properties/requir.explanation: Per-boundary upper bounds on the longest triangle edge within named boundary groups (quality.boundaries in mesh-summary.json). Use it with nearBoundaries to confirm that local refinement was actually achieved. Each entry must name a distinct declared boundary group.
/properties/refinement/properties/requir.label: Boundary maximum edge lengths

/properties/refinement/properties/requir.explanation: One boundary requirement: the longest edge of any triangle in the named boundary group must not exceed maximum.
Name of the boundary group to check: boundaryName or one faceGroups name of the tetrahedral node. volumeName, undeclared names and repeated names fail planning with INVALID_SELECTION.
/properties/refinement/properties/requir.label: Boundary group

/properties/refinement/properties/requir.explanation: Largest allowed edge length of the triangles on that boundary group (inclusive). Set it slightly above the matching nearBoundaries size when you only want to confirm that the local sizing took effect.
/properties/refinement/properties/requir.label: Maximum boundary edge

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Maximum relative discrepancy between the selected planar group triangle area and its CAD area: abs(meshArea-CADArea)/CADArea. Unitless, default 1e-10, bounded above by 0.02; numerical absolute roundoff allowance is 1e-8 mm². Keep the strict default for polygon faces. Explicitly use an engineering area-loss budget for circular or annular caps, whose straight boundary chords cannot have exact CAD area. Refine size when it fails. This does not relax plane membership or volumeTolerance, and is not a maximum pointwise surface-distance guarantee.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.defaultMeaning: Require the established strict planar polygon area agreement.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Three-dimensional tetrahedral generation choice: delaunay (default, Mesh.Algorithm3D=1) or hxt (=10). Both produce first-order tetrahedra and use the same size, boundary and independent verification contracts. This unitless choice changes the meshing method, not the acceptance criteria; compare measured quality instead of assuming one is superior.

Boolean controlling Gmsh Mesh.Optimize during generation, true by default. It enables Gmsh tetrahedral quality optimisation; false skips that option. It is unitless and does not guarantee a minimum mean ratio. Inspect measured quality or declare refinement requirements. Native readback records the selected value; HXT may also perform algorithm-internal improvement.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.defaultMeaning: Enable the standard Gmsh optimisation option.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3.explanation: Constructs a full right circular cylinder as one solid for tetrahedral meshing. origin is the centre of the starting disk, axis chooses a positive world direction, radius and height are in millimetres. Use this for rods and cylindrical specimens without a CAD file; choose hollowCylinder for a through bore. The host independently checks CAD volume pi*r²*h, analytic bounds and radial containment of every mesh node. The solid is consumed by tetrahedral; it is not separately published. Linear triangles approximate circular caps and the lateral surface.
pitfalls: A target mesh size is not a geometric-error guarantee; inspect the independently measured volume error.
Named circular or annular planar caps require an explicit areaTolerance; the strict default detects their discretisation loss.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Selects cylinder as the solid-source operation. This literal operation name is unitless; use the tetrahedral node to generate publications.
Dimensions and placement of this cylinder solid, in millimetres. Omitted members use the field defaults; unknown native options are refused.

Centre of the starting circular or annular cap in world x/y/z millimetres, default [0,0,0]. It is not the bounding-box minimum corner; the opposite cap is height along the selected positive axis. Face-group coordinates are absolute world coordinates.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.defaultMeaning: The starting cap is centred at the world origin.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.explanation: One coordinate in the ordered [x,y,z] world vector, in millimetres; each component is between -100000 and 100000. The vector default supplies zero for all three coordinates when the field is omitted.

Positive world direction of the cylinder length: x, y or z, default z. This is a unitless direction choice, not an angle or arbitrary vector; radius spans the other two axes. Changing axis also changes the cap planes to select.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.defaultMeaning: The cylinder extends along positive z.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.explanation: Outer radius of the circular cross-section (or ball), in mm, default 5, between 0.001 and 100000. This is half the diameter. For a hollowCylinder it must exceed innerRadius by at least 0.001 mm. Very large solids or small mesh sizes can exceed the bounded work estimate.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.defaultMeaning: A 5 mm outer radius is used.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.explanation: Positive distance between the two cap planes in mm, default 10, between 0.001 and 100000. Length extends along the selected positive axis from origin; this is not an absolute end coordinate.
Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/4.explanation: Constructs a straight annular solid by subtracting a coaxial through cylinder from a larger cylinder, consuming both tools and requiring exactly one resulting volume. Use it for tubes and sleeves without authoring a boolean tree. origin is the starting annulus centre; axis is positive x, y or z. radius is the outer radius, innerRadius the bore radius; their difference must be at least 0.001 mm. Independent verification checks pi*(radius²-innerRadius²)*height, bounds and each node against the outer radius and bore. Both curved walls remain in the remainder boundary group unless planar caps are named; there is no separate inner-wall selector.
pitfalls: A target mesh size is not a geometric-error guarantee; inspect the independently measured volume error.
Named circular or annular planar caps require an explicit areaTolerance; the strict default detects their discretisation loss.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/4/properti.explanation: Radius of the coaxial through bore in mm, default 3, between 0.001 and 100000. It must be at least 0.001 mm smaller than radius; zero is not a bore and requires cylinder instead. The bore spans the complete height and leaves one annular solid.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/4/properti.defaultMeaning: A 3 mm through-bore radius is used.

Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5.explanation: Constructs one complete spherical solid from a centre and radius in millimetres for tetrahedral meshing. Use it for spherical specimens and curved-boundary resolution studies. The host independently checks 4*pi*r³/3, analytic bounds and radial containment of every mesh node. It is a full ball, with no polar cuts, shell thickness or planar caps. Linear boundary triangles inscribe an approximation; choose a small enough mesh size to meet volumeTolerance.
pitfalls: A sphere has no planar faces; keep its surface in the remainder group.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Selects sphere as the solid-source operation. This literal operation name is unitless; use the tetrahedral node to generate publications.
Dimensions and placement of this sphere solid, in millimetres. Omitted members use the field defaults; unknown native options are refused.
Centre of the complete sphere in world x/y/z millimetres, default [0,0,0]. Bounds are centre minus/plus radius on each axis; this is not the minimum corner.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.defaultMeaning: The sphere is centred at the world origin.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.explanation: One coordinate in the ordered [x,y,z] world vector, in millimetres; each component is between -100000 and 100000. The vector default supplies zero for all three coordinates when the field is omitted.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.defaultMeaning: A 5 mm outer radius is used.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.explanation: Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Up to 12 named physical wall groups (shared with faceGroups: faceGroups plus cylinderGroups together may not exceed 12), each holding every whole analytic cylindrical CAD face that lies on one cylinder aligned with a world axis. Groups receive tags after the planar groups, in declared order. Use them to name a bore, a shaft or a sleeve's outer wall so loads, constraints or heat flux can be applied by name later. When planar and cylinder groups together name the whole boundary, the remainder group (tag 2) is empty and absent; the mesh then has no unnamed surface.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Cylindrical wall groups
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: [] (no cylinder groups; curved walls belong to boundaryName, as before).
pitfalls: A literal radius or centre goes stale when the solid changes; reference one shared value with $document so selector and solid stay together, or planning refuses with INVALID_SELECTION at that selector.

Only typed analytic cylinders with a world-axis direction are selectable. Cones, spheres, B-spline approximations of cylinders and oblique cylinders are not; see cadSurfaces in mesh-summary.json for what the CAD actually contains.
Two groups may not describe the same cylinder, and a box or sphere has no cylindrical wall.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: One named cylinder selector. Every whole CAD face lying on the cylinder with this axis, centre line, radius and material side joins the group. Verification then classifies every boundary triangle from its coordinates, proves each triangle is on that cylinder and faces the stated side, and measures the wall's chord deviation and unrolled area.

Name of the wall group as written to the MSH and mesh-summary.json. ASCII letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter; unique across the volume, the remainder boundary, every faceGroups name and every cylinderGroups name.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Wall group name
pitfalls: VTU files carry only the numeric tag; keep mesh-summary.json for the name map.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: World axis the cylinder is parallel to (x, y or z). The CAD cylinder's axis direction must match within 1e-9 in either sign; oblique cylinders are not selectable.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Cylinder axis
pitfalls: An oblique cylinder, even with the right radius, matches nothing and is refused with INVALID_SELECTION and a candidate list.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Any point on the cylinder's axis line, in world millimetres. Its component along axis is ignored, so a primitive's origin can be pasted or referenced unchanged. The two transverse components locate the axis.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Axis point
pitfalls: Using the centre of a different bore of the same radius selects nothing. After STEP import, check cadSurfaces in mesh-summary.json for the exact transverse position.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: One world coordinate of the axis point, in millimetres.
Cylinder radius in millimetres. The CAD face radius plus the axis-line offset must agree with this value within tolerance.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Radius
pitfalls: A bore diameter is twice the radius.
Changing the solid's radius without changing this value is refused when the solid is a primitive; for STEP the native selection refuses with candidates.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Which side of the wall is material. outer: material lies inside the radius (a shaft, rod or a sleeve's outside). inner: material lies outside the radius (the wall of a bore). Checked natively by classifying probe points either side of the wall, and again from the mesh by each wall triangle's adjacent tetrahedron, so swapped names are caught.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Material side
pitfalls: A bore is inner even though it is the inside of a tube; a sleeve's outside is outer.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Radial and axis-line tolerance in millimetres for matching a CAD face and for classifying mesh vertices. Mesh vertices sit on the CAD wall to about 1e-15 mm, so the default leaves large margin.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Match tolerance
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.defaultMeaning: Default 1e-6 mm, the same as planar faceGroups; range 1e-6 to 1e-3.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Maximum relative difference between the wall's unrolled mesh area and its CAD area: abs(unrolledArea-CADArea)/CADArea. The unrolled area (arc length times axial height, from vertex angles) is exact for a full or axis-normal-rimmed wall, so the default is tight (measured error about 1e-15). Unitless; raise it only for a wall whose rim is not an axis-normal circle or axial line (for example an obliquely trimmed face). This is different from chord deviation: the flat facets of a cylinder always lose area, and that loss is reported as maximumChordDeviation, not hidden here.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Unrolled area tolerance
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.defaultMeaning: Default 1e-9: require the unrolled mesh area to equal the CAD wall area.

/properties/refinement/properties/requir.explanation: Requirement that each named cylinder wall's maximum chord deviation stays within a limit. Chord deviation is the largest gap, over the wall's triangles, between the true cylinder and the flat facet, measured from the mesh coordinates alone: radius minus the nearest approach of the triangle's projection to the axis. For an N-sided regular prism it equals radius*(1-cos(pi/N)). The refinement loop shrinks the target size until every listed wall meets its limit or a stopping rule applies.
/properties/refinement/properties/requir.label: Cylinder chord deviation
pitfalls: Only cylinder group names are valid; planar or remainder names are refused.
A tight limit on a large part may hit the cell budget; the study then ends with STUDY_REQUIREMENTS_NOT_MET and no mesh is exported.

/properties/refinement/properties/requir.explanation: One cylinder wall and its allowed chord deviation.
Name of a cylinderGroups entry. Names must be distinct and refer to cylinder walls.
/properties/refinement/properties/requir.label: Wall name

/properties/refinement/properties/requir.explanation: Largest acceptable chord deviation in millimetres, inclusive. A 16-segment circle has about 0.019*radius deviation; 36 segments about 0.0038*radius.
/properties/refinement/properties/requir.label: Maximum chord deviation
pitfalls: Smaller is not automatically better: deviation falls roughly with the square of the edge length, so halving it costs about 1.4 times the elements around the circle and more through the volume.
